transcript:
Header:
Date: Mon Jan 18 2027 17:00 - 18: - approx 55 min
Duration: 55 minutes
Location: All-hands (virtual) - Zoom
Attendees: Avery Chen (CEO), Priya Patel (CTO), Marcus Ruiz (VP Eng), Elena Novak (Head Product), Samir Khan (Dir SRE), Kai Morris (Head People) + company

Summary:
Quick leadership check-in covering Q1 priorities, an ops post-mortem, a hiring snapshot, product experiments, and a short AMA. Tone: pragmatic, a few hard asks, recognition for ops on recent incident.

Topics:
- Q1 priorities and tradeoffs
- Reliability post-mortem (Jan 10 incident)
- Cost and model-efficiency experiments
- Dedicated / Private deployment demand signal
- Hiring and hybrid work policy
- AMA / employee questions

Action items (reported inline)

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Alright good afternoon folks, uh, thanks for joining. We'll kick off the command dock and — I keep saying soundcheck — leadership soundcheck. Uh quick run through, 55 minutes, we'll save time for questions at the end.
[00:28] Priya: Hi, everyone. A few things from infra, and then Marcus will walk through the Dedicated roadmap.
[00:45] Marcus: Hey all, short on slides, long on facts. Q1 we are focusing on three things: stability, throughput, and cost per token. We have already pulled two engineering sprints to land KV cache improvements, and that should help tail latency on long-chat scenarios.
[01:12] Elena: Quick note — product will be trialing two inference profiles on beta customers: one is latency-first and one is cost-first with aggressive quantization. We'll measure quality regressions with our eval suite.
[01:38] Samir: On the Jan 10 incident — thank you to the on-call team — root cause was an autoscaler race condition interacting with the burst policy, and a fallback didn't trigger because the routing table had inconsistent model tags. We're writing the post-mortem now.
[02:05] Avery: Thanks Samir. Please, make sure the post-mortem includes customer impact, timeline, and follow-ups. We'll expect it by the 20th.
[02:20] Kai: For people updates, hiring is on, but slower than planned. We're re-prioritizing IC roles over managers for Q1 to get velocity back. Also rolling out clearer hybrid guidelines next week.
[02:42] [03:05] Speaker 6: question in the chat — is Dedicated still on track for the March pilot?
[03:15] Marcus: Yes, pilot is still on track but with narrower scoping. We'll support one model family and two capacity tiers for the pilot so we can validate autoscaler behavior under real customer load.
[03:45] [04:00] Priya: technical — kernel selection has improved perf by 12% in our synthetic tests, but the real world is messier. We need more signal from running models with typical sequence length distributions. Please engage with the perf harness.
[04:30] Elena: Also, remember that Optimize suggestions are now available in console beta; it will propose batching and quantization settings for routes. Feedback welcome.
[04:50] [05:10] Avery: high level — our tradeoff remains: do we push customers to use cached prefixes and optimized routes aggressively, or do we default to the most compatible path? I think we need to give customers clearer cost/latency knobs.
[05:45] Marcus: Noted. We will add a config toggle in the console that surfaces cost delta and latency SLO impact before applying the routing policy.
[06:05] [06:30] Samir: On the incident timeline — at 02:14 UTC on Jan 10 we saw autoscaler thrash, CPU saturation on a subset of nodes and a subsequent model fallback failure. The circuit breaker didn't trip because the error type didn't match our current list, so traffic kept routing.
[06:58] Priya: that's a good callout — our classifier for error taxonomy needs to be more inclusive. We'll add a fallback to detect resource-saturation signatures.
[07:20] [07:45] Elena: can I ask — did we see customer-visible latency spikes or just increased 5xx errors?
[07:55] Samir: both, but the most visible was request timeouts for chat sessions longer than 5k tokens. Some customers reported slow streaming and dropped connections.
[08:20] [08:45] Avery: ok, acknowledgement — send comms to affected customers with root cause once the PM is ready. Marcus and Priya, coordinate.
[09:05] [09:30] Kai: quick people note — we got a lot of gratitude messages for the on-call team; planning a small offsite recognition and thank-you.
[09:50] [10:10] Audience: (crosstalk) thank you to SRE team!
[10:28] Priya: switching to cost story — overall infra spend is up 7% month-over-month; a lot of that is model size and increased seq lengths. The Optimize tooling suggestions can cut per-token cost 10-20% for some workloads.
[10:58] Marcus: experiment one is a batching strategy that favors slightly higher latency for much lower p95 cost. Experiment two is quantization profile swap for half the model variants. We'll run both in staging this week.
[11:28] Elena: product is prioritizing the quantization experiments for a set of BI customers who opted in. We'll collect human evals before pushing to general availability.
[11:50] [12:10] Avery: question from Slack — are we leaning into private on-prem customers or pushing hosted?
[12:22] Marcus: both — market signals show strong demand for Dedicated and Private for regulated customers. Our core motion remains hosted first for PLG, Dedicated for predictable large customers, Private for air-gapped/regulatory.
[12:50] Priya: technically, private deployments require more automation in the control plane; we're working to make that same runtime API available in VPC/on-prem with managed connectors.
[13:12] [13:40] Audience Q: "How are we handling security/compliance asks? SOC2?"
[13:48] Samir: SOC 2 Type II rolling, ISO scope work ongoing, KMS/HSM integrations in progress. We'll publish an updated compliance pack in the partner docs repo.
[14:10] Avery: thanks. Also strategic note — competitors are noisy with pricing promotions; don't panic. Our strength is being predictable and developer-friendly. Keep pushing quality of SDKs and docs.
[14:40] [15:00] Elena: product spotlight — small teams can now create per-route traces in the console and pin prompt sets to evaluate regressions. This is already used by three early customers.
[15:28] Priya: engineering spotlight — thank you to the runtime team for the new KV caching behavior; it's reducing cold-start tokens for a subset of flows. Please keep logging edge cases.
[15:55] [16:15] Avery: hiring — we are opening a small apprenticeship program for SWE interns, see the internal link. Also we will be more conservative on vendor spend.
[16:42] Kai: benefit update — parental leave policy clarified, and new learning stipend is live next month.
[17:05] [17:30] Audience question: "Will there be a follow up Q&A doc?"
[17:36] Avery: yes, we'll capture FAQs and answers in the all-hands notes and share.
[17:50] [18:10] Marcus: short engineering note — we will freeze non-critical experiments for two weeks while we validate the autoscaler changes. This is to prevent more surface area during the Dedicated pilot.
[18:35] Priya: also adding more canaries and a heavier tracing sample rate for the next week.
[18:55] [19:20] Elena: product will pause feature flags that touch routing logic until the autoscaler changes are in.
[19:45] [20:00] Audience: question in chat about OKR alignment — are we reworking the Q1 goals?
[20:12] Avery: minor tweaks only. We'll publish a short addendum to the Q1 goals with two new metrics: "mean cost per token for tail workloads" and "end-to-end latency SLO adherence".
[20:40] [21:05] Kai: please fill the anonymous survey about hybrid working and meeting density. Results will be shared.
[21:28] [21:50] Recognition: shoutout to on-call: Janelle, Omar, and Priya (the SE rotation helped)
[22:10] Priya: back to a technical ask — we need owners to opt into the perf harness; I will email the list.
[22:30] [23:00] Audience: brief applause / chat gifs
[23:18] Avery: roadmap ask — Marcus, can you make the Dedicated pilot success criteria explicit?
[23:30] Marcus: yes: 99.5% uptime during pilot, latency p95 below 350ms for the latency tier, and a validated autoscaler under burst traffic. Also verified fallback policies that don't surface errors to customers.
[24:00] [24:30] Avery: good. Elena, product success metrics?
[24:38] Elena: adoption of pilot by three anchor customers, NPS uplift on private offerings, and zero regressions on critical prompt sets.
[24:58] [25:20] Audience: question — will we open-source any of the runtime improvements?
[25:29] Priya: maybe smaller components, but the full runtime won't be open-sourced right now. We will continue to publish research notes and perf guidelines.
[25:50] [26:15] Samir: security note — we're adding an automated audit for RBAC changes in control plane, that'll alert when a policy widens privileges.
[26:40] [27:05] Avery: final quick AMA — put questions in chat, we'll answer a subset live.
[27:28] Audience Q: "When can we expect the cost dashboards to be updated?"
[27:35] Elena: next week beta refresh with per-route breakdowns by token class.
[27:58] Audience Q: "Will there be more office meetups?"
[28:10] Kai: yes, micro-hubs are being curated, details next week.
[28:30] [29:00] Rapid-fire: 
- "Any risk of layoffs?" Avery: No planned reductions. We are optimizing hiring.
- "Can we get more training?" Kai: yes, new stipend and learning hours soon.
[29:45] [30:10] Avery: closing notes — gratitude, clear asks for PMs and Eng leads to review the post-mortem, and for people managers to be visible and supportive next two weeks.
[30:35] Marcus: one last technical — please label routes with typical sequence length distribution, that metadata is critical for kernel selection and batching.
[31:00] Priya: and please opt in to higher sampling for traces this week.
[31:28] [31:50] Action item recap (verbal): Priya to schedule kernel deep dive; Marcus to finalize Dedicated scoping; Samir to publish incident post-mortem; Kai to share hybrid guidelines; Avery to circulate Q1 slide addendum.
[32:20] [33:00] Final Qs (chat) and short answers.
[33:30] Avery: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned — recording and notes will be posted.

Post-meeting notes:
- Post-mortem due 2027-01-20 (engineering + SRE)
- Q1 addendum due 2027-01-25 (Avery)
- Hiring proposal due 2027-01-29 (People)
- Console Optimize beta feedback due 2027-02-05 (Product + Eng)

End of transcript.
